proven by URL-building tests for both sources\u0022,\u0022As a backstop against a filter the API ignores, each source rejects a record whose per-listing condition field says new (auto.dev: the record\\u0027s condition property; marketcheck: the listing\\u0027s inventory_type property) with its own rejection reason naming the VIN (for example \\u0027candidate rejected, new car\\u0027), and a record with no such field is kept as before; proven by source tests over fixtures that include one new and one used listing, cut from the existing fixtures under tests/Odonomics.Tests/fixtures/sources (the marketcheck one already holds inventory_type new rows)\u0022,\u0022The search\\u0027s per-source summary line counts these among rejected as it does other rejections; the README\\u0027s search section says both APIs are asked for used cars only and that a record marked new is dropped, with the scenario\\u0027s year and mileage facets unchanged; dotnet build and dotnet test succeed with zero warnings; commits are small with conventional messages, no em dashes, no AI attribution\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Brian\\u0027s ruling 2026-09-26 (relayed by run session odonomics-59): new cars are never candidates; no marking option, exclude at the source. Rejections go to SourceResult.Rejections (IListingSource.cs). Existing tests: tests/Odonomics.Tests/Sources/AutoDevSourceTests.cs and MarketcheckSourceTests.cs with fixtures under tests/Odonomics.Tests/fixtures/sources/auto.dev and /marketcheck, where auto.dev records carry condition used and marketcheck listings carry inventory_type new or used. The walk\\u0027s equivalent rule is in WalkCommand.cs (cars.com cards titled New are skipped, and a detail page reading as a new car is dropped as a new-car listing); the README\\u0027s walk section describes it. Do not change the year or mileage facets. Task 48b0414f (placeholder price rejection in the same two gates) is in flight; rebase onto it if it merges first and keep both rejections as separate reasons.
